items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I mean it’s all music. It’s all music. It wouldn’t surprise me if Bach were alive today that he’d be a jazz musician.

ctx.x: I just noticed that struck me, because I was reading “Dear John Coltrane” your poem, and it says, “In the dead of night I’m writing poetry in another hotel room and J.S. Bach is on the radio.” And I went back and read that again, because the title, “John Coltrane,” and you’re listening to J.S. Bach. It was a nice juxtaposition.

Yeah, yeah. I mean it’s all music. It’s all music. It wouldn’t surprise me if Bach were alive today that he’d be a jazz musician. He was a great improviser after all and I think probably that may be how he did most of his compositions. For a man to write that many cantatas can’t possibly have been sitting there putting it all down. I think he improvised a lot of music and had people copied it for him as he played. That was a guess I got from a composer of my acquaintance. But at any rate, yeah, I think that there…
Do you feel that that might be one reason why jazz requires more of listeners than most pop music?
